record.original_question: Let N be a finite-index subfactor of a tracial matrix ultraproduct M_U = ∏_{n→U} M_n(C). Must N itself be isomorphic to a matrix ultraproduct?

evidence.quote: Problem 5. Let N be a finite index subfactor of the matrix ultraproduct MU. Then is N also isomorphic to a matrix ultraproduct?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix a free ultrafilter $\mathcal{U}$ on $\mathbb{N}$, and let
$$M_{\mathcal{U}} \;=\; \prod_{n\to\mathcal{U}} M_n(\mathbb{C})$$
denote the tracial ultraproduct of the full matrix algebras $M_n(\mathbb{C})$ (each equipped with its normalized trace), so $M_{\mathcal{U}}$ is a $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor with the trace inherited from the ultralimit of the normalized matrix traces. A "matrix ultraproduct" means a $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor of the form $\prod_{n\to\mathcal{V}} M_{k_n}(\mathbb{C})$ for some sequence of positive integers $k_n\to\infty$ and some free ultrafilter $\mathcal{V}$ on $\mathbb{N}$.

Suppose $N \subseteq M_{\mathcal{U}}$ is a subfactor of finite Jones index, i.e. $N$ is a $\mathrm{II}_1$ subfactor with $[M_{\mathcal{U}} : N] < \infty$.

Question: Must $N$ itself be isomorphic (as a tracial $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor) to a matrix ultraproduct?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as one of fifty open problems on ultraproduct II_1 factors. Web searches turn up related results on closedness of index values for subfactors of ultraproducts and on central sequence subfactors, but no resolution of whether a finite-index subfactor of the matrix ultraproduct is itself a matrix ultraproduct. No published proof or counterexample was located.

status_evidence.snippet: Problem 5. Let N be a finite index subfactor of the matrix ultraproduct M_U. Then is N also isomorphic to a matrix ultraproduct?
status_evidence.claim: Listed as an open problem in a compilation of fifty open problems on ultraproduct II_1 factors.

status_evidence.title: Closedness of Index Values for Subfactors
status_evidence.snippet: For inclusions of finite factors with bounded indices and trivial relative commutants, the W* ultraproduct yields an inclusion whose index is the ultralimit of the original indices.
status_evidence.claim: Related results on finite-index subfactors and ultraproducts exist, but do not resolve whether such subfactors of a matrix ultraproduct are themselves matrix ultraproducts.
